answer: A person who intentionally gives false evidence in any stage of a judicial proceeding is committing an offence under Section 229(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which can result in imprisonment for up to seven years and a fine. If the false evidence is given in a case other than specified in subsection (1), it falls under Section 229(2), which carries a punishment of up to three years of imprisonment and a fine. Additionally, if false evidence leads to the wrongful conviction and execution of an innocent person, the penalty can be severe, including death or the punishment specified in subsection (1).
